quote:
Side Letter, Section 6.1 (Governing Law for indemnification: Delaware)
- Side Letter, Section 6.2 (Jurisdiction for indemnification: Delaware Court of Chancery) ... The Side Letter routes all indemnification disputes to Delaware under Delaware law, while the SPA and Escrow Agreement are governed by New York law and committed to New York courts. ... There is a risk of inconsistent rulings ... Seek to conform the Side Letter's governing law and jurisdiction to the SPA (New York law, New York County courts).
reason: Issue 4 identifies the conflict. Side Letter Section 6 picks Delaware law and the Court of Chancery for indemnification disputes, while SPA Sections 11.8 and 11.9 pick New York law and New York County courts. It explains why this matters: indemnity claims are split from other disputes, costs rise, and rulings may be inconsistent. It recommends conforming the Side Letter to New York, which matches the expected fix. One weakness: Issue 4 itself never cites Section 11.11. It does treat the Side Letter as controlling (it 'routes all indemnification disputes to Delaware'), and Issue 3 states that the Side Letter has first priority under Section 11.11. The precedence point is therefore covered in substance, though not tied to this issue explicitly.
